title: Tadla irrigated plain, Beni Moussa side on 20 Oct 2026
summary: On 20 Oct 2026 the radar shows the irrigated Tadla plain inside a 9 km circle, where changing fields cover 9.6% and rough dry ground and fields 42.5%. This date carries a flag for a backscatter shift, so its values are less reliable than those of an unflagged date.

sections.heading: What the radar shows here
sections.text: The circle averages -5.64 dB in HH and -16.35 dB in HV. Built-up land is the brightest type, at 3.7 dB in HH, and smooth bare ground the darkest, at -21.02 dB in HV.

sections.heading: Terrain types and what they mean
sections.text: Changing fields, 24.35 km2, are the plots whose HV moved most during the season; on this date they sit at -16.93 dB in HV and -8.85 dB in HH. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes, 22.6% of the circle, give the strongest HV, -13.67 dB, from leaves and branches. Smooth bare ground, 49.29 km2, is dark in both channels, -13.39 dB in HH, because dry, smooth soil reflects the pulse away.

sections.heading: Data quality notes
sections.text: One flag applies: backscatter over built-up land shifted more than 0.5 dB from its June-September median, a possible processing offset or widespread wet conditions. Possible cause: a processing offset in this product; reprocessed files would settle it. Possible cause: rain wetting soil and walls; rain records would check it. One track only, so slopes facing away from the radar can fall in shadow.
